criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), explicit users (marine/conservation scientists), strong need rationale with quantified context and four literature references. Could state mission objectives/requirements more formally, so not a 9–10.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with week-by-week tasks, deadlines and task narratives tied to course material (astrodynamics, launch, orbit). However, no explicit contingency provision for project variations, and the plan contains a technical error (see issues), capping it below Accomplished.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
Strategies: The goal is to brainstorm and research as many possible strategies for the satellite’s launch/orbit

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is limited to background reading and STK tutorials; no preliminary results, calculations or simulations are presented. The only technical design statement (600 km 'geostationary') is incorrect, and no interpretation of results is given.

evidence.quote: My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear logical structure with headings, well-written prose, consistent formatting, labelled Gantt chart with legend, and numbered references matching URLs. Slightly short of top marks as references are bare URLs without proper citation formatting.

technical_issues.issue: 'Geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km' is wrong: GEO is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO and cannot be fixed above the reef. Also GEO is unsuitable for high-resolution reef imaging.
No contingency/variation provision in the plan, as the rubric's Accomplished level expects.
References are bare URLs rather than properly formatted citations.

overall: Strong, well-referenced mission concept for GBR bleaching monitoring with a detailed Gantt-chart plan and STK selected. Weakened by a fundamental orbit misconception (600 km 'geostationary'), thin preliminary progress (tutorials only), and no explicit source list or contingencies.

feedback.summary: A strong, well-referenced concept for a GBR bleaching-monitoring mission with a clear user need, a detailed Gantt-chart plan and STK selected. To reach higher marks, correct the orbit misconception (600 km is LEO, not GEO), add contingencies to your plan, list your information sources explicitly, and present preliminary technical results rather than tutorials alone.
next_steps: Correct the orbit analysis: GEO is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO. Evaluate which orbit actually suits high-resolution reef imaging (e.g. revisit time vs resolution trade-offs) and justify the choice technically.

Add contingency/variation provisions to your project plan (e.g. buffer weeks, fallback strategies if STK simulations or data access fail) and explain why the plan is structured this way for this mission.

Include an explicit list of planned information sources (literature, databases, software documentation) with properly formatted citations, and present at least one preliminary result or calculation with brief interpretation before the next milestone.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly states the mission purpose (near-real-time GBR bleaching monitoring), identifies users (marine and conservation scientists), and supports the need with quantified context and four literature references — well done. To reach the top band, state mission objectives and requirements more formally (e.g. numbered, measurable requirements) and link each to user needs. Also replace bare URLs with properly formatted citations.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart with week-by-week tasks, deadlines and task narratives tied to course material is detailed and credible. However, the plan lacks contingency/variation provision, which the Accomplished level requires, and it contains a technical error: a 'geostationary orbit at 600 km' is not possible (GEO is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO). Fix the orbit reasoning and add fallback strategies to lift this criterion.
criteria.C3: Progress to date is limited to background reading and STK tutorials 1–4, with no preliminary results, calculations or simulations presented. The only technical design statement (600 km GEO) is incorrect. For a higher mark, include a preliminary set of results — e.g. an initial orbit/coverage analysis in STK or a link-budget estimate — with brief description and interpretation.
criteria.C4: Your report is clearly structured with logical headings, well-written prose, consistent formatting, and a well-labelled Gantt chart with a legend. References match between text and list. To reach the top level, replace the bare URLs with properly formatted citations in a consistent referencing style.
